action: After any web server compromise, remove the GSocket client, its persistence and staged files, then confirm relay connections have stopped. Apply deny-by-default outbound rules and audit cron entries, systemd units and shell startup files.
attack: T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
exec: Patching a hacked web server is not enough; a relay tool left behind keeps attackers in, and it has no fixed address to block.
plain: Microsoft warns that hackers who break into Linux web servers are leaving behind a free relay tool that keeps them connected even after the original hole is fixed.

key_findings: Internet-facing Linux web servers are the target; PHP applications and cPanel hosting account for 63.9% of incidents and Apache for 24.3%.
Education and research is the most affected sector at 30.7% of organisations, which Microsoft attributes to exposure rather than deliberate targeting.
After web application code execution, a curl download-and-run script installs GSocket, which connects outbound to a shared public relay.
Access persists after the original flaw is patched, and there is no attacker-owned address or domain to block.
GSocket detections rose 356.2% from March to August 2026; a few intrusions also tried the Dirty Frag flaw CVE-2026-43284 to gain root.
recommendations: Remediate the host, not just the vulnerability: remove the GSocket client, persistence and staged files and confirm relay connections stop.
Apply deny-by-default egress rules and monitor connections to relay infrastructure.
Mount temporary and memory-backed directories as non-executable and alert on execution from hidden or world-writable paths.
Audit cron entries, systemd units and shell startup files.
Hunt for gs-netcat or gsocket processes and staging files under /dev/shm.

summary: Microsoft says multiple unrelated attackers are installing the open-source GSocket tool on Linux web servers after exploiting web applications. Both the server and the attacker connect outbound to a shared public relay, so there is no attacker address to block and access survives patching of the original flaw. Detections rose 356.2% between March and August 2026, with PHP and cPanel hosting most affected.
title: Microsoft: attackers use open-source GSocket to keep hidden access to hacked Linux servers

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Microsoft Threat Intelligence report.
